title: Process Power
equation: Process Power = Improvement Rate × Years Compounded × Copy Difficulty
hook: Competitors can watch exactly what you do and still not be able to do it.
statement: Some advantages live in how you work, refined for so long that copying them takes rivals years.
explainer: Some companies have let rivals tour their factories for decades and still never got copied. The edge wasn't a secret. It was years of small improvements stacked into habits.
sop: Name the processes that drive your quality, speed, or cost edge.
Rate each one's Improvement Rate from 1 to 10.
Rate its Copy Difficulty from 1 to 10.
Write it into training so it outlives any one person.
equation_example: Improvement Rate 3 × Years Compounded 10 × Copy Difficulty 8 = 240. High across the board means rivals can watch and still can't copy it. A young, easy-to-copy process, 3 × 2 × 3 = 18, barely protects you.
question: Write down one process that lives only in your head, and document it this week.
closing_statement: Build the edges that quietly get better every year.
caption:
